### `executor.await` (::catalyst::executor::AwaitOp)

_Wait for one `executor.launch_async` to finish._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `executor.await` $token attr-dict `:` type($token)
```

Block until the `executor.launch_async` that produced `token` has finished. Waiting on the
token rather than on the session means other launches on that session are left running.

#### Operands:

| Operand | Description |
| :-----: | ----------- |
| `token` | A handle to one launch that has not finished yet. |


### `executor.call` (::catalyst::executor::CallOp)

_Invoke a symbol in a previously-loaded shared library._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `executor.call` $session `(` $symbol `)` `(` $inputs `)` attr-dict
              `:` type($session) `,` functional-type($inputs, $results)
```

Invoke `symbol` in a shared library already loaded on the executor `session`.

The operand list packs input buffers followed by output buffers.
`num_input_args`, when present, marks the boundary: operands `[0, num_input_args)`
are inputs and the remainder are output buffers to be filled by the callee.
Without `num_input_args` all operands are treated as inputs.

<tr><td><code>num_input_args</code></td><td>::mlir::IntegerAttr</td><td>32-bit signless integer attribute</td></tr>
</table>

| `inputs` | variadic of memref of any type values |

### `executor.close` (::catalyst::executor::CloseOp)

_Release a session handle with an executor._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `executor.close` $session attr-dict `:` type($session)
```

Release the `session` previously established via `executor.open`, marking the end of its use

#### Operands:

| Operand | Description |
| :-----: | ----------- |
| `session` | A handle to an open executor session. |


### `executor.launch_async` (::catalyst::executor::LaunchAsyncOp)

_Dispatch a `()->()` entry on the executor without waiting for it._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `executor.launch_async` $session `(` $kernel_callee `,` $object `)` attr-dict
              `:` type($session) `->` type($token)
```

Like `executor.launch`, but returns as soon as the entry has been started instead of waiting
for it to finish; the entry runs on a background thread on the host. Pass the returned token
to `executor.await` to wait for it.

</table>

### `executor.launch` (::catalyst::executor::LaunchOp)

_Dispatch a cross-compiled kernel on the executor and receive its results._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `executor.launch` $session `(` $kernel_callee `,` $object `)` `(` $inputs `)` attr-dict
              `:` type($session) `,` functional-type($inputs, $results)
```

Invoke, on the given `session`, the kernel previously registered via
`executor.send_binary`. The `inputs` operand list mirrors the original host-side
`func.call` to the kernel; `results` mirrors the kernel's return values.

### `executor.open` (::catalyst::executor::OpenOp)

_Open a session with an executor._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `executor.open` `(` $address `)` attr-dict `:` type($session)
```

Establish a connection to the executor reachable at `address` and return an
`!executor.session` handle identifying it. Subsequent executor operations consume the handle
to target this session.

### `executor.send_binary` (::catalyst::executor::SendBinaryOp)

_Ship a compiled kernel object file to the executor._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `executor.send_binary` $session `(` $binary_path `)` attr-dict `:` type($session)
```

Transfer the compiled binary at `binary_path` over the `session` to the executor.
The executor loads the file and exposes all of its symbols.
`format` selects the wire encoding for the transfer, which is handled by the
runtime. Defaults to `0` (the raw object file); other values are reserved for
future encodings.

<tr><td><code>format</code></td><td>::mlir::IntegerAttr</td><td>32-bit signless integer attribute</td></tr>
</table>

#### Operands:

| Operand | Description |
| :-----: | ----------- |
| `session` | A handle to an open executor session. |
